etymology: Latin: “you too” - the second-person form of the two-wrongs move, and the most common sentence on the internet.
committed_when: A criticism has been made that one cannot answer on the merits.
tell: The reply is a counter-accusation, and the original charge is never mentioned again.
counter: Concede the point about consistency and keep the charge on the table - both can be true, and only one was asked about.
senses: Answering a charge by charging the accuser with the same thing, as though a second offence cancelled the first.
It works because hypocrisy is genuinely relevant to credibility, so the deflection has a real foothold. The foothold is about the speaker; the question was about the act.
example: “You are funded by a billionaire.” “So are you.” Both disclosures are true; only one of them was on the table.

confused_with.tell: Tu quoque attacks the accuser's consistency; two wrongs uses the comparison as a defence of the act itself.
